Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're ready to schedule the index backfill and want to lock down a warmstart protocol that avoids a cold-query blast to our vector DB (VectraDB hosted) and prevents a temporary regression in ranking quality. High level constraints from our side:

- Corpus size: ~520M documents (~1.2TB after embeddings)
- Online search p95 target: < 120ms
- Rerank model runs client-side and expects stable top-100 pass-through from the vector store
- We have a short maintenance window (02:00–06:00 UTC) that we'd prefer to use for major migrations if possible

Questions we need Redwood's help on:
1) A recommended warmstart/priming pattern for the first-wave index so we don't spike latency when traffic hits previously cold partitions.
2) Suggested smoke/eval metrics for rerank sanity checks (we care about MRR, Recall@10, and also exact-match rate on a seeded set).
3) Any vector-DB compatibility gotchas (IDs, float32 vs int8 quantized vectors, sharding/replica impact) we should preflight before export.

Attached our current index snapshot export (stub) and a short sample rerank testset. Happy to jump on a call to triage.

Thanks,
Hannah

Hannah — thanks for the clear constraints, this is exactly the right level of detail. Short answers up front, then a proposed next step:

- Warmstart approach: staged wave backfill + targeted query priming. We recommend seeding top-K cache entries and a small set of representative queries during off-peak, then opening traffic to a canary shard.
- Rerank smoke metrics: baseline MRR, Recall@10, and a differential that flags >5% drop in MRR or >8% drop in Recall@10 vs current production for the seeded testset. Also track latency delta at p95 for the full stack.
- Vector DB preflight: make sure external IDs map 1:1 (no rehashing), confirm vector dtype (we prefer float32 during ingest then a controlled quantization pass), and check traceroutes for replica-sync lag.

Proposed next step: 30m call tomorrow to confirm wave sizes, sample queries for priming, and owners. I'll invite Marissa (implementation lead) and Ben (CS escalation) to flesh out the operational checklist. If that works, we'll produce a short M-A-P and timeline.

Availability: 2026-11-10 09:00–12:00 PT or 2026-11-10 14:00–16:00 PT. Let me know what works.

— Grace

Thanks — took notes from the call and drafted an operational checklist below. Attaching a lightweight manifest and the rerank test CSV for your team (stubs attached).

Operational checklist (wave 0 -> wave N):

1) Export compatibility & preflight (owner: Searchly impl) — Before any ingest:
   - Confirm external_id -> internal_id mapping (no collisions).
   - Validate vector dtype and dimensions (expected 768 dims); if using quantization, produce a quantization map and sample vectors to validate relative distance preservation.
   - Share index_backfill_manifest.json (attached) with shard counts and doc ranges.

2) Snapshot ingest to a staging cluster (owner: Redwood infra) — safe window only:
   - Create staging cluster with same shard/replica config as prod but single traffic route.
   - Ingest first 10% (wave 0) using small batches (<= 10k vectors / batch) to avoid long queueing spikes. Track ingestion throughput and replica lag.

3) Cache priming & query seeding (owner: Searchly + Redwood CS) — during off-peak:
   - Run priming script with ~2k representative queries (we'll collaborate on selection). For each query, call the vector-store and cache the top-200 ids into Redwood's prefix cache.
   - Run a small rerank pass on those results and store metrics. This primes the end-to-end path and warms KV caches.

4) Smoke tests and rerank eval (owner: Redwood QA + Searchly QA):
   - Compare seeded-testset metrics vs baseline: report MRR, Recall@10, Precision@5, and p95 latency for rerank. Flag if MRR delta > 5% or Recall@10 delta > 8%.
   - Run A/B on 1% of traffic to validate production behavior for 24 hours. Collect error rates and latency distributions.

5) Canary cutover and incremental waves (owner: Redwood CS + Searchly Ops):
   - If smoke passes, open 10% traffic to shard group for 6 hours, monitor traces. Incrementally increase in 20% steps with 1–2 hour observation windows.
   - Provide automatic rollback if error rate > 1% or latency spike > 50% at p95.

6) Full cutover & post-cutover checks (owner: Searchly Ops):
   - After full ingestion, re-run priming script across the full query sample and validate final metrics. Schedule a 48-hour observation window for manual checks.

Timing estimates (rough):
- Wave 0 (10% ingest + priming + smoke): 6–10 hours
- Wave increments (per 20%): 3–6 hours each depending on ingest throughput
- Full backfill (end-to-end): depends on ingest parallelism — estimate 5–7 days if we use a 4x ingest cluster scale-up

Vector DB considerations we recommend you confirm now:
- Replica sync semantics (how long between primary write and all replicas seen by queries)
- Support for stable IDs on upserts vs full reindex
- Any per-request rate limits and throttling behavior during priming

Attachments (stubs): rerank_testset_v2.csv — seeded queries + expected judgments; index_backfill_manifest.json — doc ranges, shard plan; mutual-action-plan.docx — proposed owners & dates.

Next immediate asks (owners + deadlines):

- Redwood: provide priming script and sample query list by 2026-11-12 (owner: Marissa)
- Scheduling: tentative wave 0 window 2026-11-18 02:00–10:00 UTC (confirm by 2026-11-12)

If Searchly confirms manifest today, we can pre-stage the staging cluster and run a dry ingest of a small sample to validate the pipeline.
